name: Syria
headline: After the war, everything remains to be rebuilt.
summary: Syria is emerging from more than a decade of civil war and the fall of the Assad regime in December 2024. The institutions, the currency, and the infrastructure are deeply destroyed. The absence of a rating, of CDS, and of reliable data is not a detail: it is the heart of the risk.

history.title: The French mandate
history.text: The League of Nations entrusts Syria to France. Modern borders and centralized administration take shape on a fractured territory.

history.title: Independence
history.text: French troops leave the country. A period of political instability opens, marked by coups and regional rivalries.

history.title: The Baath seizes power
history.text: The Baath Party installs an authoritarian regime, secular at first but dominated by the Alawite minority. The army and intelligence services become central.

history.title: Hafez al-Assad
history.text: Bashar's father takes power in a coup. He maintains a balance of patronage, repression, and alliances with the USSR then Iran.

history.title: Revolution and war
history.text: Arab Spring protests are repressed. The country slides into an internationalized civil war, with the Islamic State, Russia, Iran, and Turkey.

history.title: Russian intervention
history.text: Moscow intervenes militarily to save the regime. Airstrikes allow Damascus to retake part of the territory.

history.title: The fall of the Assad regime
history.text: A lightning rebel offensive ends fifty years of family rule. The country enters an uncertain transition, without reliable institutions or a stable currency.

institutions.executive: Transitional authorities; legitimacy and scope still disputed
institutions.central_bank: Central Bank of Syria, capacity limited by sanctions and the currency shortage
institutions.currency: Syrian pound (SYP), multiple market rates and steep depreciation
institutions.law: An inheritance of French civil law; courts and administration to rebuild
institutions.fact: No active sovereign rating, no quoted CDS, uncertified public accounts: risk is first an information risk.

allies.name: Russia
allies.note: Historic military support; naval and air bases to negotiate.

allies.name: Iran
allies.note: Support for the fallen regime; now contested influence.

allies.name: Turkey
allies.note: Support for rebel groups and the Kurdish issue.

rivals.name: Jihadist groups
rivals.note: A security threat and fragmented territorial control.

dependencies.name: International aid
dependencies.note: Reconstruction, food, and medicine depend on donors.

dependencies.name: Turkey
dependencies.note: Trade, energy, and control of armed factions.

dependencies.name: Sanctions
dependencies.note: Access to the global financial system remains constrained.

gdp_growth.note: War and transition prevent any durable recovery. The estimate itself is fragile without reliable national accounts.

inflation.note: Inflation is fed by the pound's depreciation, shortages, and transaction costs. Prices vary sharply by region.

debt_gdp.note: External debt is largely in default or undocumented. The ratio should be read as an order of magnitude, not a certainty.

policy_rate.note: The policy rate shapes only part of credit, so dollarized and informal is the economy.

unemployment.note: Half of the active population is estimated jobless or underemployed. Youth and women are hardest hit.

reserves.note: Reserves are nearly exhausted. There is no cushion to defend the currency or fund essential imports.

rating.note: No active rating. The absence of a note is not neutral: it reflects the impossibility of assessing the ability and willingness to pay.

cds.note: No quoted CDS. Sovereign risk has no observable price, which reinforces the uncertainty premium.

equity_index.note: The market is tiny and illiquid. Its prices are not a reliable signal about the real economy.

currency.name: Syrian pound
currency.note: The pound has collapsed and several rates coexist. Informal dollarization is households' answer to uncertainty.

strengths: A geographic position at the crossroads of the Levant.
A diaspora and dispersed technical skills.
Reconstruction needs that can attract capital if peace holds.
risks: A violent political transition and unconsolidated institutions.
A destroyed currency, sanctions, and a crippled financial system.
A total absence of reliable data and market prices.
opportunities: A gradual reintegration into regional trade.
Sanctions relief conditioned on a credible transition.

quiz.question: Why is the absence of a rating and of CDS so important for Syria?
options: It deprives the investor of any price for risk
quiz.explanation: Without a note or a CDS, no market prices sovereign risk. GeoCapital treats this void as maximum risk, not as an absence of risk.
